concept: The Sunday Problem / a customer testimonial for ROTA
genre: single-voice customer testimonial case study with burned-in transcript captions
why_this_use_case: Interview is the one use case on the shortlist with measured plates and no delivered film. Loop one scored interview_veo_v1 at 8.5/10 and recorded an explicit open caution - speaker identity across a longer exchange remains untested - which four films later is still open. The Chowdeck reference is the commercial form of exactly that: one recurring speaker across several setups, burned-in transcript captions on every frame, a brand mark, and product b-roll between the lines.
why_this_routing: Dialogue goes to Veo 3.1 Fast with audio, the only tested model that produced clean speech with no burned-in subtitles. It bills $0.15/s at 1080p, the same as 720p, so this loop takes the free resolution upgrade loop one did not know about. Identity across the exchange is handled the way loop four handled it: one hero plate, then image-to-video from a single frame of it. Whether that survives with audio and lip-sync is the open question, so it is probed with one paid shot before the rest are bought. Faceless hands go to Kling; silent b-roll goes to Veo at the silent rate.
speaker: a woman in her forties with warm olive skin and greying dark hair tied back, wearing a flour-dusted charcoal apron over a cream shirt
setting: seated in her bakery, a warm wood-and-tile wall behind her, out-of-focus shelves of bread and a window of morning light to one side

runs.line: We're a bakery. Six people, two ovens, and a lot of very early mornings.
runs.hypothesis: Does double duty: it is the opening testimonial line and it supplies the single frame every later line is generated from. Eight seconds for a fourteen-word line, because loop one measured delivery running short of the requested length in every trial.

input.prompt: A documentary customer testimonial interview, filmed as clean camera footage. A woman in her forties with warm olive skin and greying dark hair tied back, wearing a flour-dusted charcoal apron over a cream shirt, sits in her bakery facing slightly off-axis to camera, a warm wood-and-tile wall behind her with out-of-focus shelves of bread and a window of soft morning light to one side. Eye-level medium close-up, static camera, shallow depth of field, warm natural light. She speaks directly and warmly, as if answering an off-camera question. AUDIO: she says in natural British English, unhurried, with a small pause after the first sentence: "We're a bakery. Six people, two ovens, and a lot of very early mornings." She finishes speaking with roughly a second to spare and holds a relaxed, thoughtful expression. One small hand gesture only. Quiet room tone, no music. Clean photographic frame with no captions, subtitles, titles, logos or graphical text of any kind.
